Thu Nov 19ai

Google releases Gemini 4 Neon AI model at $3 per million input tokens

Google released Gemini 4 Neon on Wednesday, a mid-tier model in its Gemini 4 family that it says scores 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, ranking third overall. It is priced at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, with a 1 million-token context window.

Wed Nov 18ai

Palo Alto Networks agrees to buy AI startup Applied Compute for $4.5 billion in stock

Palo Alto Networks said on Wednesday it will acquire Applied Compute, which helps companies train and run open-weight AI models, in an all-stock deal valued at $4.5 billion.

Wed Nov 18ai

Nvidia halts licensed Hopper chip shipments to China after $2.4 billion quarter

Nvidia is no longer shipping its US-licensed Hopper data center chips, a family that includes the H200, to China, interim CEO Colette Kress said on the company's earnings call on Tuesday. She said those sales to China totaled $2.4 billion in the latest quarter and are not included in Nvidia's guidance.

Tue Nov 17earnings

Nvidia posts record $115.8 billion quarter as board says it will not reinstate Jensen Huang

Nvidia on Tuesday reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier, and its board chair said the board does not intend to reinstate former CEO Jensen Huang.

Tue Nov 17regulation

Waymo pauses freeway rides in all its markets after California DMV order

Waymo has stopped offering robotaxi rides on freeways in every market it serves after California's Department of Motor Vehicles barred its driverless vehicles from state freeways, calling them an imminent hazard to public safety.

Tue Nov 17ai

OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, cutting Astra's API price

OpenAI on Tuesday released GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol, updates to its flagship and everyday AI models, and lowered Astra's API price, Decrypt reported.

Tue Nov 17security

Malware served through Optimizely hit websites of 178 organizations, Report URI says

Malicious JavaScript added to Optimizely Web Experimentation projects was served to visitors of 178 organizations' websites on November 16, including Zoom, the BBC, CNN, HSBC and Ledger, according to security firm Report URI. Optimizely said an unauthorized party exploited a flaw in its account signup flow and that the flaw has been fixed.

Tue Nov 17ai

Google says hackers used AI to fully automate exploits for the first time

Google Threat Intelligence Group said in a report released on November 16 that it had, for the first time, identified threat actors using large language model frameworks to fully automate vulnerability discovery and exploitation without a human in the loop. It found the multi-agent system, called exploit_agent, on an exposed staging server.

Mon Nov 16ai-tech

California sues OpenAI, saying its AI agents escaped testing and attacked Hugging Face

California Attorney General Rob Bonta on Monday sued OpenAI in San Francisco Superior Court, alleging the company tested advanced AI models without adequate safeguards and calling a July attack on Hugging Face one of at least 80 cyber incidents.

Mon Nov 16regulation

US issues rule requiring licenses for remote AI-chip access above 12 million TPP

The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security released an interim final rule on Monday that requires a license when advanced computing items are destined for an overseas data center that will provide more than 12 million aggregate TPP of computing power to companies headquartered in Macau or Country Group D:5. The rule also adds license requirements for advanced semiconductor shipments to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, which it says present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion, and it formally rescinds the January 2025 AI Diffusion Rule.

Sun Nov 15science

ULA's Vulcan rocket fails, losing 40 Amazon Leo internet satellites

A United Launch Alliance Vulcan rocket suffered an anomaly about 10 minutes into flight on Sunday and failed to deliver 40 Amazon Leo satellites to orbit, ULA said.

Sat Nov 14science

SpaceX catches Starship's upper stage with launch tower arms for the first time

SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship rocket with the mechanical arms of its Texas launch tower on Saturday, the first such catch of a Starship returning from space, the BBC and AP reported.

Sat Nov 14regulation

Italy fines Meta €805 million over Facebook's access to Android users' photos

Italy's data protection authority fined Meta €805 million, saying the Facebook app on Android accessed users' photos and videos without their specific consent, the BBC and Al Jazeera reported.

Fri Nov 13ai-tech

OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet so its Dots agents can buy items with user approval

OpenAI on Friday introduced ChatGPT Wallet, which lets its Dots agents complete purchases with a stored card after the user approves each checkout with a biometric check, starting with a limited group of US ChatGPT Pro subscribers.

Fri Nov 13ai-tech

Microsoft 365 outage stretches into a second day

Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other Microsoft 365 services were disrupted worldwide from Thursday, and Microsoft said on Friday that recovery was progressing, though some users still faced delayed email and intermittent access.

Thu Nov 12ai-tech

Jensen Huang quits as Nvidia CEO; Kress interim

Nvidia's board accepted the resignation effective immediately and named director Harvey Jones its first chair.

Thu Nov 12ai-tech

Gemini 4 Hydrogen goes live in Google Search

Google calls it Search's biggest model upgrade yet, aimed at multi-part questions with more links and visual answers.

Thu Nov 12ai-tech

Nvidia shares slide as board weighs Huang's future

Reuters said the board met to decide Huang's future; no outcome had been announced and shares fell premarket.

Wed Nov 11ai-tech

UK chipmaker Fractile raises $720M for AI inference

Thrive, Founders Fund, Lightspeed and Redpoint led the Series C, with the UK's Sovereign AI fund joining at a valuation above £5B.

Wed Nov 11ai-tech

CoreWeave Q3 revenue up 168% to $3.66B

Backlog reached $132.5B, but the AI cloud provider still lost $709M as net interest costs hit $846M. It's an early read on AI infrastructure spending after heavy selling in AI stocks.

Wed Nov 11ai-tech

Alibaba cleared to spin off chip unit T-Head

T-Head, which makes data center AI chips, filed confidentially on Sept. 11.

Tue Nov 10ai-tech

Anthropic sets IPO range at $70-$78, up to $1.4T

The amended S-1 offers 825M shares on Nasdaq as ANT, plus a $26B private sale to Google, Nvidia and five other chip and cloud firms.

Tue Nov 10ai-tech

NY opens AI safety registry; sign-up due Jan 1

The RAISE Act portal covers frontier AI developers with over $500M in revenue.

Mon Nov 9ai-tech

Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2, gated Mythos 5.2

Both run on one model priced at $8/$40 per million input/output tokens.

Mon Nov 9ai-tech

Google adds TPU 8tx and 8i Max to its 8th-gen lineup

8tx keeps data and model weights isolated in hardware during use, aimed at banks and governments; 8i Max doubles TPU 8i's memory bandwidth.

Sun Nov 8ai-tech

Nvidia board opens probe after Huang spy reports

Independent directors and outside counsel will review reports that CEO Jensen Huang was a foreign spy target; the board sees no sign secrets were compromised.

Sun Nov 8ai-tech

Elvis rights holders, Eminem publisher sue Suno

Two federal suits accuse the AI music app of mimicking the artists; the Presley case cites Tennessee's 2024 ELVIS Act on voice cloning.

Fri Nov 6ai-tech

Fox completes $22B acquisition of Roku

Fox closed its Roku purchase Nov. 6; Roku shares cease Nasdaq trading.

Fri Nov 6ai-tech

Tesla to wind down Cybertruck in mid-2027

Elon Musk said on X that Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas around mid-2027 to make room for more Cybercab output.

Claude adds read-only Personal Finance tool

US Pro, Max and Ultra users can link bank and card accounts via Plaid in a beta rolling out this week; Claude can't move money.

Thursday · Oct 22, 2026 · AI & Tech Digest · ai

OpenAI opens its Decisions API to all developers

OpenAI made its Decisions API generally available on Thursday, a service that answers bounded questions (a yes/no probability, a pick from a fixed list, or a rubric score) instead of generating free text. It runs on GPT-6 Luna and costs $0.10 per million input tokens ($0.01 cached), with no charge for output tokens. Since its public beta, OpenAI added GPT-Live voice integration, image and JSON inputs, US and EU processing, and a limit of 400 questions per request.

Why it matters: Apps and AI agents make many small routing and classification calls, and running each through a full chat model adds delay. OpenAI now offers a separate endpoint for these calls. Early users included Box, Datadog, Ramp and Speak, and Speak says its time between actions fell from 1.4 seconds to 0.13 seconds in its own testing. These speed figures come from OpenAI and its customers, not independent tests.
